newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, February 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, February 4.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Eurostat, the EU statistical body, said its decision regarding the treatment of interest on zero coupon bonds and postal bonds would trim 0.26 percent from Italy's projected deficit to GDP ratio. The Italian government said this meant the European Commission's forecast of its 1997 budget deficit would be cut to 3.0 percent from 3.3 percent, qualifying it for the single currency (all).
* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi hailed preliminary data that point to a state sector surplus of two trillion lire in January 1997 as proof the government is on the right track (all).
* Trade unions threatened to strike against a plan to reform state railway company Ferrovie dello Stato put forward by the government (all).
* Metalworkers trade unions and employers are expected to give their response today to a new government proposal to settle a long-running pay dispute (all).
* France Telecom does not rule out buying a stake in information technology group Olivetti "if this is the only way to become strong in Italian telecommunications" (all).
* Italian bonds and the lira weakened as result of comments from the Davos economic summit indicating that Germany and business leaders don't want Italy in the first wave of Emu (all).
* State oil company ENI said its total investment in the 1997-2000 four-year period will be 35 trillion lire, of which 90 percent will be in energy production (Sole 24 Ore).

* In an interview, Thomas Bartlett, chairman of Bell Atlantic Corp, which recently bought a 8.26 percent stake in the Omnitel Sistemi Radiocellulari consortium, says its group will "seriously consider any chance to further increase its stake" in the consortium (La Repubblica).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
